risks: We do not have long-term agreements with a majority of our customers.
We do not have firm, long-term supply agreements with most customers and primarily rely on purchase orders rather than fixed-term contracts.
As a result, our customers may amend, reschedule, reduce, or cancel purchase orders prior to finalisation.
Such changes could disrupt our production planning, lead to sub-optimal capacity utilisation, and adversely affect our revenues, margins, working capital and cash flows.
Some customer purchase orders include provisions for remedies such as liquidated damages or specific performance in the event of delay or default.
The loss of this significant or key customer or a reduction in the amount of business could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

A reduction in these segments may result from factors such as changes in government procurement policies, budget allocations, adoption of new technologies, increased competition, or shifts in customer preferences.

We are dependent on a limited number of suppliers for procurement of our raw materials, and the loss of any one or more of our major suppliers would have a material adverse effect on our business operations and profitability.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: The Company describes itself as a non-manufacturing procurement, assembly and integration business rather than a vertically integrated manufacturer. Our Business, 'PLANT & MACHINERY, EQUIPMENTS': 'Since, we are not a manufacturing unit, we are mainly engaged in the supplying of Forensic products and assembling of different equipment's and Kits.' BACKWARD LINKAGE: forensic systems and evidence-collection tools are procured through a combination of imports and domestic sourcing. Imports began with Sirchie (USA), from whom the Company 'has obtained representation Certificate ... in India to solicit orders for Sirchie Fingerprint Laboratories'; current OEM engagement is via 'Non-Exclusive distributorship agreement with renowned international OEMs or deal in Purchase order basis', with named OEMs Sirchie (USA), Thermo Fisher Scientific, Invitrogen, Rapiscan Systems, Smallpond, MHC Hardware Software Trading LLC and Seratec. Source countries are stated as 'China, USA, Turkey, Japan, Italy etc.' Import substitution is quantified: the Company 'sourced approximately 65.42%, 85.72% and 91.35% of its raw material requirements locally in the financial years ended March 31, 2024, 2025 and 2026 respectively'; the corresponding procurement table prints Forensic Products & Kits Imported of Rs. 501.39 lakhs / 34.58% (FY24), Rs. 629.01 lakhs / 14.28% (FY25) and Rs. 6,43.82 lakhs [printed thus] / 8.65% (FY26), against domestic purchases of Rs. 948.41 lakhs / 65.42%, Rs. 3,774.42 lakhs / 85.72% and Rs. 6,802.24 lakhs / 91.35%, on total purchases of Rs. 1,449.80 / 4,403.43 / 7,446.06 lakhs. Purchases of Goods represented 85.01%, 81.75% and 54.76% of total expenditure and 70.44%, 67.72% and 48.03% of revenue from operations in FY26, FY25 and FY24 respectively (total expenditure Rs. 8,758.90 / 5,386.43 / 2,647.56 lakhs). LIMITED FORWARD/IN-HOUSE INTEGRATION: kits are assembled in-house at the registered office; handheld-device software development is 'outsourced to third parties under non-disclosure agreements (NDAs)' and hardware integration/assembly is 'either outsourcing ... or do in-house'; fuming chamber and cabinet manufacturing and assembling is outsourced; and from mid-FY25 the Mobile CSI Vehicle model shifted to 'supplying only the digital and scientific kits and outsourcing the vehicle procurement and fabrication work to the local dealers', which the Company states 'reduces capital intensity and working-capital blockage'. Both software prototypes initiated in FY26 (AI-Powered Judicial Assistance Platform, LIMS) were likewise developed 'by outsourcing the development work to a third party, based on the concept and framework developed by the R&D team of Kwick'. LOGISTICS: a dual model - direct delivery from import custom house to customer location for high-value/time-sensitive imported equipment, and central dispatch from the Company's office-cum-warehouse for stocked and pre-assembled kits - executed through third-party (3PL) certified logistics providers. Two return-on-equity measures printed in the same chapter move in opposite directions. RoNW (Basis item 4) rises: 28.75% (FY2024), 30.68% (FY2025), 32.62% (FY2026). ROE in the KPI table falls net over the same span and is non-monotonic: 41.43% (FY2024), 45.34% (FY2025), 38.98% (FY2026). The denominators differ — RoNW is stated against year-end net worth, ROE against 'Average Total Equity' — so the two are not required to agree, but any downstream consumer treating them as interchangeable would draw opposite conclusions. Recorded, not resolved.

The RoNW definition note is circular as printed: 'Return on Net Worth (%) = Net profit after tax, as restated / Return on Net worth as restated as at period/year end.' The denominator reads 'Return on Net worth' where 'Net worth' is evidently intended. Note (iii) immediately following does define 'Net worth' properly. Reproduced as printed; not corrected.

The weighted-average RoNW note defines the aggregation as '[(Net Worth x Weight) for each financial year] / [Total of weights]' — i.e. weighting Net Worth rather than the RoNW percentage — while the table's own column being averaged is RONW (%). overview.business_model: The Company earns revenue in two stated streams: (i) Sales of Goods, covering four product segments — Forensic Science & Physical Evidence Solutions (fingerprint powders, brushes, lifting tapes and kits, footprint and impression kits, alternate light sources, handheld devices, laboratory instruments, evidence-collection kits for explosives, narcotics, blood, body fluids and gunshot residue, ballistics and scene-documentation kits, plus refill consumables), Mobile CSI Vehicles (mini and macro mobile forensic vans/laboratories and motorcycles fitted with scientific kits), Cyber & Digital Forensics (mobile and computer data retrievers, social-media analysis tools, virtual forensic computing platforms, digital kits, forensic imagers, write-blockers) and DNA Forensics (DNA sample-collection kits, sexual-assault evidence kits, genetic analyzers, DNA database systems, Rapid HT and SmallPond, for which the Company states it is an authorised non-exclusive reseller in India); and (ii) Sales of Services, principally a rental/sub-lease model for handheld scanners used by enforcement agencies for liquor detection and other forensic detection, scanning and imaging equipment, bundled with manpower support where required, plus AMC and other services. Operating training and post-delivery support by telephone, online/remote assistance and on-site visits is provided across all four product segments. Stated customers are police stations, central and state forensic laboratories, central and state fingerprint bureaus, crime investigation departments, police training academies and institutions, and universities offering forensic science courses; client acquisition is stated to be primarily through GeM (Government e-Marketplace) and other e-procurement portals. genesis.founding_story: Incorporated in 2005 by Mr. Shammer Saralal Shah with an initial focus on software development — 3D rendering, animation and simulation — serving the construction sector through 3D walkthroughs. In 2008 the Company identified opportunities for forensic training and developed an Interactive Virtual Reality Crime Scene Simulator for training and proficiency testing of personnel responsible for crime scene management, for which it states it received substantial support and funding from the Ministry of Science & Technology, the Directorate of Forensic Science and TIFAC (Technology Information, Forecasting and Assessment Council). The simulator was designed to train personnel in police training schools, forensic colleges and academies. From FY2015 the Company expanded into fingerprint science and thereafter into forensic sciences, cyber/digital forensics, social-media and big-data analytics, specialising in handheld field devices that help investigators identify visible/invisible evidence and digitise it in a tamper-evident manner to support evidentiary integrity for court admissibility. The business is led by Mr. Shammer Saralal Shah (Founder & Managing Director), assisted by Mr. Tulsidas Hinduja Ashok kumar (Chief Operating Officer). My reasoning: it is dated three days before the RHP, it bears on who holds the stock at listing, and the document offers no explanation at all. The opposite decision, which I think is genuinely defensible, is to lead with the RoC order - a concluded, quantified regulatory finding against the Company and its Managing Director for a decade of trading outside its own objects clause - whereas the 39.9% is OUR arithmetic on two printed totals and comes with an express instruction that no lock-in breach may be alleged. A reviewer who weights adjudicated facts above unexplained ones should swap 1 and 2.

RED FLAG 3: customer decline versus board churn. I made 'customers 128 to 124 to 95 while revenue tripled' the third red flag, which pushes board instability (five exits in eleven months, independent directors serving five days and nine days) to fifth and therefore off the dashboard. The opposite decision was to elevate board churn into the top 3, changing the reader's first impression from growth quality to governance. I chose growth quality because the customer count is the single fact that most directly tests whether the reported earnings are durable, but the five-day and nine-day independent directorships are arguably the more unusual disclosure in absolute terms, and I am not confident this is right.

RED FLAG 4: the BRLM related-interest disclosure. I placed the Corporate CapitalVentures / CCV Emerging Opportunities Fund-I unitholding fourth. The opposite decision was third: it is the only conflict of interest at the offer level, it names both the director and the fund, and the fund it names is one of the allottees inside red flag 1 (2,81,224 down to 1,56,224), so the two arguably belong adjacent at the top. I scored 4 on the absence of any capex object, the General Corporate Purposes amount printing as a placeholder, and the absence of both a monitoring agency and any external appraisal. The opposite decision was 6, on the ground that all three absences are regulatorily permitted for a fresh issue below the Regulation 262 threshold of Rs. 5,000 lakhs and are affirmative disclosures rather than defects - so a 4 partly penalises the issuer for a lawful structure. I am also uneasy that a low score on this parameter could be misread as a pricing judgement. It is not one: this document contains no price band, and nothing in any basis string is a proxy for one.

products.body:

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: The Company describes itself as a non-manufacturing procurement, assembly and integration business rather than a vertically integrated manufacturer. Our Business, 'PLANT & MACHINERY, EQUIPMENTS': 'Since, we are not a manufacturing unit, we are mainly engaged in the supplying of Forensic products and assembling of different equipment's and Kits.' BACKWARD LINKAGE: forensic systems and evidence-collection tools are procured through a combination of imports and domestic sourcing. Imports began with Sirchie (USA), from whom the Company 'has obtained representation Certificate ... in India to solicit orders for Sirchie Fingerprint Laboratories'; current OEM engagement is via 'Non-Exclusive distributorship agreement with renowned international OEMs or deal in Purchase order basis', with named OEMs Sirchie (USA), Thermo Fisher Scientific, Invitrogen, Rapiscan Systems, Smallpond, MHC Hardware Software Trading LLC and Seratec. Source countries are stated as 'China, USA, Turkey, Japan, Italy etc.' Import substitution is quantified: the Company 'sourced approximately 65.42%, 85.72% and 91.35% of its raw material requirements locally in the financial years ended March 31, 2024, 2025 and 2026 respectively'; the corresponding procurement table prints Forensic Products & Kits Imported of Rs. 501.39 lakhs / 34.58% (FY24), Rs. 629.01 lakhs / 14.28% (FY25) and Rs. 6,43.82 lakhs [printed thus] / 8.65% (FY26), against domestic purchases of Rs. 948.41 lakhs / 65.42%, Rs. 3,774.42 lakhs / 85.72% and Rs. 6,802.24 lakhs / 91.35%, on total purchases of Rs. 1,449.80 / 4,403.43 / 7,446.06 lakhs. Purchases of Goods represented 85.01%, 81.75% and 54.76% of total expenditure and 70.44%, 67.72% and 48.03% of revenue from operations in FY26, FY25 and FY24 respectively (total expenditure Rs. 8,758.90 / 5,386.43 / 2,647.56 lakhs). LIMITED FORWARD/IN-HOUSE INTEGRATION: kits are assembled in-house at the registered office; handheld-device software development is 'outsourced to third parties under non-disclosure agreements (NDAs)' and hardware integration/assembly is 'either outsourcing ... or do in-house'; fuming chamber and cabinet manufacturing and assembling is outsourced; and from mid-FY25 the Mobile CSI Vehicle model shifted to 'supplying only the digital and scientific kits and outsourcing the vehicle procurement and fabrication work to the local dealers', which the Company states 'reduces capital intensity and working-capital blockage'. Both software prototypes initiated in FY26 (AI-Powered Judicial Assistance Platform, LIMS) were likewise developed 'by outsourcing the development work to a third party, based on the concept and framework developed by the R&D team of Kwick'. LOGISTICS: a dual model - direct delivery from import custom house to customer location for high-value/time-sensitive imported equipment, and central dispatch from the Company's office-cum-warehouse for stocked and pre-assembled kits - executed through third-party (3PL) certified logistics providers. NIL DISCLOSURE: 'We have not entered into any technical or other collaboration as on date.'

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body: AFFIRMATIVE DISCLOSURE - not seasonal. MD&A, item 8: 'Our Company's business is not seasonal. However, the business of the Company does depend on country's economy situation and inflation.' The DRHP does, however, identify tender-cycle timing as a driver of period-to-period variation: 'Tender/award timing and order-book conversion' and 'Customer concentration: Share of revenue from a few large departments/states and timing of their procurement' are both listed under 'FACTORS AFFECTING OUR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS', and Business Strategy 5 states that 'revenue contribution from individual states may vary from year to year depending on tender cycles, order execution and customer procurement timelines'.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- We do not have long-term agreements with a majority of our customers.
- We do not have firm, long-term supply agreements with most customers and primarily rely on purchase orders rather than fixed-term contracts.
- As a result, our customers may amend, reschedule, reduce, or cancel purchase orders prior to finalisation.
- Such changes could disrupt our production planning, lead to sub-optimal capacity utilisation, and adversely affect our revenues, margins, working capital and cash flows.
- Some customer purchase orders include provisions for remedies such as liquidated damages or specific performance in the event of delay or default.
- The loss of this significant or key customer or a reduction in the amount of business could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
- A reduction in these segments may result from factors such as changes in government procurement policies, budget allocations, adoption of new technologies, increased competition, or shifts in customer preferences.
- We are dependent on a limited number of suppliers for procurement of our raw materials, and the loss of any one or more of our major suppliers would have a material adverse effect on our business operations and profitability.
